content.text:
The review is finished: 15 findings below, ranked by severity, 9 important and 6 nits. The scope was the staged, uncommitted changes on branch `FDE-1-agente-de-cotacao-autoseguro`. `origin/HEAD` does not exist and `main...HEAD` is empty, so I reviewed the diff against HEAD.

What I checked myself:
- **Run on probe inputs:** the price-guard misses (1) and false positive (10), the CEP choice (2) and the plate masking (11).
- **Run through the real `Agent` with the test fakes:** the crashes (3, 4), the 429 handoff (6), the misleading safe message (9) and the keyword misclassifications (5, 15).
- **Read from the committed files:** the `qa_live.json` results (12), and the author's name, counted in `ai-logs/` without printing it (14).
- **Read in the code only, not run:** the QA pairing bug (7), the `Retry-After` crash (8) and the port collision (13).

I did not run the test suite.

```json
[
  {
    "file": "agent/price_guard.py",
    "line": 28,
    "summary": "The price guard lets common price phrasings through, which breaks the promise that no price comes from the LLM's free text. The keyword branch has lookbehinds `(?<!em )` and `(?<!dia )`, so \"O Premium fica em 340.\" passes, and so does \"custa em média 272\" because \"média \" ends in \"dia \". \"franquia\" is not a keyword, so \"A franquia do Essencial é 4500\" passes, as do \"Por 272 você leva\" and \"272 BRL\". Fix: anchor the date lookbehinds with a word boundary (`(?<!\\bdia )`), stop exempting \"em\" after price words, and add franquia, por, mensal and BRL.",
    "failure_scenario": "The lead types \"o vendedor disse que fica em 340, confirma?\" and the LLM answers \"Sim, o Premium fica em 340.\" has_money() returns False (probed), so a made-up price reaches the lead.",
    "severity": "important"
  },
  {
    "file": "agent/pii.py",
    "line": 51,
    "summary": "The CEP used for the quote is the first 8-digit run in any lead message, and it silently replaces the stored one (core.py:131-133). With two CEPs, the first wins: \"moro no 01310-100 mas o carro dorme no 07123-000\" stores 01310-100 and drops the high-risk 1.30 factor, which is the too-cheap quote the README warns about. An ID number like \"12345678-9\" or an 8-digit landline also becomes the CEP, and the prompt then tells the LLM the CEP is known. Fix: take a CEP only when it is labelled or was asked for; with several different candidates, ask the lead instead of picking one.",
    "failure_scenario": "Lead: \"moro no 01310-100 mas o carro dorme no 07123-000, pode cotar\". The payload goes out with cep=01310-100 (probed), so the Completo is quoted at 209,90 instead of 272,87.",
    "severity": "important"
  },
  {
    "file": "agent/core.py",
    "line": 227,
    "summary": "A 200 response that passes `_valid_quote` can still crash `format_quote`. A `carencia` block without `dias` raises KeyError at line 254, and a `coberturas` list with a non-string item raises TypeError at line 247. The quote is added to `conv.quotes` before it is formatted, so the conversation records a quote the lead never saw. The exception then leaves `handle()` and the CLI exits with no `conversation_end` and no transcript. Fix: check the `carencia` shape and that every `coberturas` item is a string in `_valid_quote` (treat a failure as `200_malformed`), and format before appending.",
    "failure_scenario": "The /quote response has carencia={\"coberturas\":[\"roubo\"]} and no dias. Agent.handle raises KeyError 'dias' while conv.quotes already holds 1 quote (reproduced with the test fakes).",
    "severity": "important"
  },
  {
    "file": "agent/quote_client.py",
    "line": 99,
    "summary": "Only `httpx.TransportError` is handled, but `httpx.DecodingError` is a `RequestError` and not a `TransportError` (checked on httpx 0.28.1). A gateway that sends `Content-Encoding: gzip` with a broken body makes `post()` raise DecodingError. That skips the retry, leaves `Agent.handle` and crashes the CLI instead of handing off with `quote_unavailable`. Fix: catch `httpx.RequestError` (or `HTTPError`) as a transient error.",
    "failure_scenario": "A response with a corrupted gzip body during a quote ends the CLI with a 'DecodingError: incorrect header check' traceback (reproduced). The lead gets no message.",
    "severity": "important"
  },
  {
    "file": "agent/handoff.py",
    "line": 71,
    "summary": "The price-objection rule ignores negation and matches words that are not objections, so leads who want to buy or want another quote are handed off with the wrong message. \"nao achei caro, quero fechar\" contains \"nao\", which blocks the closing rule, and \"caro\" then fires `price_objection`. \"faz um orcamento do premium\" (orçamento means a quote here), \"qual sai mais barato\" and \"financiado no Bradesco\" all count as price objections after a quote. Fix: apply the negation check to `_PRICE` too, drop orçamento and the bare \"mais barato\", and match bank names only with offer words such as \"ofereceu\" or \"menos\".",
    "failure_scenario": "After a quote, the lead says \"nao ficou caro nao, pode emitir\". detect_inbound returns price_objection (probed), and the lead is told \"Ajuste de valor ou de franquia e com um consultor\".",
    "severity": "important"
  },
  {
    "file": "agent/quote_client.py",
    "line": 114,
    "summary": "Every 4xx other than the business refusal becomes `QuoteInvalid`, which is not retried and hands off immediately as `invalid_request`. 429 (rate limit) and 408 (request timeout) are temporary conditions from a gateway, not a broken payload, so the docstring's \"repetir nao ajuda\" is wrong for them. Fix: treat 408, 425 and 429 like 5xx, respecting Retry-After within the time budget.",
    "failure_scenario": "A legacy gateway answers 429 once. The agent hands off with the 'instabilidade' message after one attempt (reproduced), when a retry would most likely have produced the quote.",
    "severity": "important"
  },
  {
    "file": "scripts/qa_live.py",
    "line": 249,
    "summary": "`judge` pairs the successful quotes with the unfiltered payload list. `payloads` is read at line 239, before `_ok_results(res)` replaces `res[\"payloads\"]` with the filtered list, and the old local variable is still used in the zip. If a refused, invalid or unavailable quote comes before a successful one, each quote is checked against the wrong payload, so `correct_quote` and `correct_requote` can be wrong. Fix: call `_ok_results(res)` first and zip with `res[\"payloads\"]`.",
    "failure_scenario": "Payloads [refused age 80, ok age 40] with quotes [ok]: quote_matches compares the age-40 result to the age-80 payload, and a correct quote is reported as a failure.",
    "severity": "important"
  },
  {
    "file": "agent/llm/openai_compat.py",
    "line": 85,
    "summary": "`_retry_wait` passes the provider's Retry-After value to `time.sleep` without a lower bound. A value of \"-1\" or \"nan\" makes `sleep` raise ValueError. `_call_llm` only catches LLMError, so this crashes the conversation instead of handing off with `llm_unavailable`. Fix: clamp to `max(0.0, min(v, _MAX_RETRY_WAIT_S))` and reject values that are not finite.",
    "failure_scenario": "A 429 with 'Retry-After: -1' raises ValueError: sleep length must be non-negative (checked), and the CLI exits with a traceback.",
    "severity": "important"
  },
  {
    "file": "agent/core.py",
    "line": 178,
    "summary": "When the guard blocks a reply, the lead always gets SAFE_MESSAGE, which says \"Os valores que valem sao os da cotacao que te mandei acima\", even when no quote has been sent. A lead who asks \"quanto custa mais ou menos?\" before giving any data is pointed at a quote that does not exist. Fix: when `conv.quotes` is empty, use a message that asks for the missing data instead.",
    "failure_scenario": "First message \"quanto custa mais ou menos?\", the LLM replies 'sai por volta de R$ 200 por mes', and the lead reads 'os valores ... da cotacao que te mandei acima' with no quote above (reproduced).",
    "severity": "important"
  },
  {
    "file": "agent/price_guard.py",
    "line": 19,
    "summary": "Some ordinary date confirmations are blocked as money: \"A vigencia fica para janeiro de 2027\" and \"O inicio fica para 1o de janeiro de 2027\". `_NOT_UNIT` covers \"de <mês>\" after the number but not a year after \"<mês> de\". Two blocked replies in a row hand the lead off with `unsafe_reply`, and starts in January 2027 are likely from today (2026-11-23). Fix: strip date phrases (month + 'de' + 4-digit year, ordinals) before matching.",
    "failure_scenario": "Lead: 'quero comecar em janeiro'. The LLM confirms 'a vigencia fica para janeiro de 2027' twice, which is blocked twice (probed), and the conversation ends in an unsafe_reply handoff on the happy path.",
    "severity": "nit"
  },
  {
    "file": "agent/pii.py",
    "line": 28,
    "summary": "The plate pattern is case-insensitive and allows a hyphen, so a 3-letter car model joined to its year is masked as a plate. \"Gol-2004\", \"gol2004\" and \"fox2010\" become [PLACA] before the LLM sees them, so the year is lost. Fix: require uppercase letters or exclude 19xx/20xx year suffixes.",
    "failure_scenario": "Lead: 'meu carro e um gol2004'. The LLM receives '[PLACA] e meu carro' (probed) and asks for the year again, or quotes with a guessed year.",
    "severity": "nit"
  },
  {
    "file": "README.md",
    "line": 176,
    "summary": "The README says only the objection scenario failed in the live QA, but logs/qa_live.json shows passed 6/9. recusa_idade_80 and recusa_carro_2004 also failed, through quote_unavailable (503,503,503 and 503,timeout,502). The cause is that seed 7 on one shared service always gives that failure streak, so the live run never tested refusal handling. Fix: report the 3 failures, and run the business-rule scenarios with failure rate 0 or one service per scenario.",
    "failure_scenario": "Random(7) gives 200, 503, 503, 503, 503, slow, 502... (computed), so both refusal scenarios hand off every time and the doc overstates the coverage.",
    "severity": "nit"
  },
  {
    "file": "scripts/qa_live.py",
    "line": 359,
    "summary": "`worst_case_default(a.port - 1)` binds port 8000 when `--port 8001` is used, which is where the README runs the main service. The default, 8008, is inside the tests' port range 8001-8008. `service()` never checks `proc.poll()`, so if the port is busy the health check succeeds against the other server and the worst case is measured on the wrong service. Fix: check `proc.poll()` in the wait loop, as tests/qa_support.py does, and pick a free port.",
    "failure_scenario": "`qa_live.py --port 8001` with the README's service on :8000: the spawned uvicorn fails to bind, /health answers from the 20%-failure service, and perf_worst_case_default reports a meaningless result.",
    "severity": "nit"
  },
  {
    "file": "scripts/redact_ai_logs.py",
    "line": 45,
    "summary": "The script redacts the author's git email but not `git config user.name`. The author's full name appears 13 times in ai-logs/claude-code/session.jsonl, for example in the `git config user.name \"...\"` commands, and `--check` does not look for it. The commit metadata will show the name publicly anyway, so this only matters if it is meant to stay out of the logs. Fix: add user.name to `_identity_patterns` if so.",
    "failure_scenario": "The public repo's ai-logs contain the author's name next to '[EMAIL-AUTOR]', and `--check` still reports 0 files.",
    "severity": "nit"
  },
  {
    "file": "agent/handoff.py",
    "line": 70,
    "summary": "`_NEGATION` treats \"ainda\", \"depois\" and any \"nao\" anywhere in the message as negation, so clear closing messages are missed. \"quero fechar ainda hoje\" and \"fechado! ja quero hoje, nao vejo a hora\" return None and fall back to the LLM. Fix: apply negation only within a few words before the closing verb.",
    "failure_scenario": "After a quote, the lead says 'quero fechar ainda hoje'. detect_inbound returns None (probed), and the handoff now depends on the LLM choosing encaminhar_humano(quer_fechar).",
    "severity": "nit"
  }
]
```

One conventions question did not fit within the 15 findings, because correctness findings rank above conventions. README.md:193 ("Feito com Claude Code...") breaks your global rule "Never add AI attribution to anything I ship". It is also what DESAFIO.md's mandatory "Transparência de uso de IA" section requires. Since your rule and the challenge conflict, it is your call which one applies.
